label: GPT-6 Astra
output:
Mr. Bergeron, Hélène here. You are right that people deserve a straight answer, especially when they have paid for bread in advance. I’m sorry my sign left so much room for worry. I meant to keep a happy surprise for the reopening, and instead I have my nephew showing me a thread where people think we are disappearing.

So here is the news: **Le Pétrin Doré is not closing or moving. The building was sold—to me!** We signed at the notary on December 15. After nearly 18 years of opening the bakery door on this corner, I now own the building too. I wanted to tell you with everything finished and the new oven ready, but this is certainly a good reason to tell you sooner.

And to answer the most important question right away: **every carnet is still valid, with no expiry date.** We sold 214 in October, at $60 for 12 loaves, and we will honour every loaf still owed. If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves waiting for you. The two-week closure changes nothing about that.

Every carnet holder can also have one free croissant in January, with my thanks for your patience. And if anyone would rather have their money back, please come and see me. I will give you a refund, no questions asked. You do not have to argue your case or feel uncomfortable asking.

Here are the dates, without any mysterious “big news soon” this time:

**We will be closed January 4–18 for renovation work. We reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.**

**On Saturday, January 23, everyone is invited to celebrate with us. Coffee and a piece of our new bread are free.** You don’t need a carnet, and you don’t need to be a regular. Please come in, see what we have done, and say hello.

The biggest job during the closure is replacing our oven. The old one dates from 1998 and has broken down three times this year. I have affection for many old things, but an oven that stops working when you have bread to bake tests that affection quite a bit. We have a new four-deck oven coming from a supplier in Laval. This is something I have wanted to do for a long time.

We are also taking over the space at the back that used to be the dépanneur’s storage area. There will be six small tables. Finally, you will be able to sit down! It is not a huge expansion, but for our little bakery it is a very happy change. A proper oven and somewhere to sit with your coffee—that is the “grande nouvelle” we were trying to keep a surprise.

I also want to answer the concern about the apartments, because the people upstairs should not have to read rumours about losing their homes. **All three apartments will stay rented, with the same tenants and the same rent.** I have promised this to them in writing. There is no plan to turn their homes into condos. They are our neighbours, and this good news for the bakery is not supposed to be bad news for them.

As for Mr. Ferland, he is 81 and retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered to sell the building to me before offering it to anyone else. So, Marc-Antoine, your cousin was half right: the building did sell, but the baker downstairs bought it.

Mr. Ferland has come in every morning for 17 years for his baguette, “pas trop cuite.” He cried a little at the notary. This was not just a transaction for him, and it was not just one for me either. I am very grateful that he gave me this chance. I have been here since March 2009, and buying the building is my way of being able to stay.

A word about the sign, too. My nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking about how it might look beside “closed January 4–18.” That is not his fault; I approved it. I can see now that a little more information would have saved everyone some worry.

The half-empty shelves were not a sign that we were winding down, either. We had sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches. That was the aftermath of a very busy Christmas, not a bakery preparing to disappear.

I understand why people are nervous. We have lost too many small shops in Mile End, and sometimes a paper in a window really is the first sign that another one is going. I should have remembered that before putting up ours.

But I also want to say, calmly and clearly, that the suggestion the carnets were a scam hurt me. After 17 years on this street, that is a hard thing to read. Asking what happens to your prepaid bread is completely fair. Suggesting I collected your money knowing I would not honour it is something else. I hope the answer above puts that worry to rest. Your carnets are good, your bread is coming, and anyone who wants a refund can have one.

Priya, thank you for your kind words. And thank you to everyone who defended us, checked on us, or simply worried because they would miss the bakery. Even in a thread that gave me quite a shock, it means a lot to know people care whether our door stays open.

Please come celebrate on January 23. I had imagined a different way of announcing all this, but I am happy you know now. We bought the building. We are staying. And I am very much looking forward to baking your bread in an oven that behaves itself.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
